claims.text: An array is a data structure holding a fixed number of elements of one data type under one name, with each element reached by an index between the array's lower and upper bound.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: The index is the position of an element within the array; the element is the value stored at that position, so Data[i] names the element at index i.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: An array's size comes from its declared bounds, not from a function, because LENGTH() works on strings, so the number of elements is read from the lower and upper bound.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A 1D array suits a list of values with one position each, such as a week of temperatures, whereas a 2D array suits a grid where each value belongs to a row and a column, such as a seating plan.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Choosing 1D or 2D follows the shape of the problem's data: values addressed by one position need one bound pair, and values addressed by a row and a column need two, because the structure should mirror how the data is addressed.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A 1D array is declared DECLARE <name> : ARRAY[<lower>:<upper>] OF <type>, and a 2D array with two bound pairs as ARRAY[<row low>:<row high>, <col low>:<col high>] OF <type>.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Processing an array means visiting elements by index, in a loop from the lower to the upper bound, doing the work on each element - totalling, counting, finding the largest, updating.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A linear search examines each element in turn until the target is found or the bounds are passed, and a bubble sort repeatedly compares neighbours and swaps those out of order, so the largest values bubble to the end.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).
